name: Batch File Renamer
description: Rename or change the extension of many files at once — prefix, suffix, sequence numbers or find/replace — then download them all as a ZIP.
body:
📂

Click to select files or a whole folder

Everything stays in your browser

howto: Pick a mode: change the extension, apply a name pattern, or find/replace text in names.
Select one or more files (or an entire folder) with the dropzone.
Configure the options for the chosen mode — prefix, suffix, numbering or the find/replace pair.
Preview the new filenames in the panel on the right.
Click Download renamed files to receive everything in a single ZIP.
features: Three modes: extension change, pattern rename, find/replace
Sequence numbering with custom prefix/suffix and zero-padding
Option to keep the original extension while renaming the base
Live preview of every new filename before you download
One-click ZIP export of all renamed files using JSZip

faq.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. All files are processed locally in your browser using the File API. They never leave your device.

faq.q: Does changing an extension convert the file?
faq.a: No. Renaming an extension only changes the label — it does not change the actual file format. Use the File Type Detector tool to confirm a file's real type, then convert it with the right tool if needed.

faq.q: Can I rename files inside subfolders?
faq.a: Yes. When you select a folder, files in subfolders are included, and their relative paths are preserved inside the ZIP.

faq.q: What if two renamed files end up with the same name?
faq.a: The tool automatically appends a number suffix (like _1, _2) to keep every filename unique.
